## Purpose

Integration/export services and the host-capacity services that sit outside the pipeline agent
runtime. The existing services cover GitHub handoff integration, OpenDesign content loading, and
server-side PPTX generation. [capacity_state.py](../../backend/app/services/capacity_state.py) owns pure CPU/memory admission evaluation plus the
process-local latest snapshot/decision; [host_metrics.py](../../backend/app/services/host_metrics.py) is the AWS-facing adapter that discovers
instances and obtains CloudWatch Agent readings.

The integration/export services are invoked by API routes. In production, [main.py](../../backend/app/main.py)'s lifespan
poller is the sole writer of the capacity holder; [admin_capacity.py](../../backend/app/api/admin_capacity.py), [run_commands.py](../../backend/app/api/run_commands.py), and
`handoff.py` are readers. [capacity_state.py](../../backend/app/services/capacity_state.py) imports neither boto3 nor [host_metrics.py](../../backend/app/services/host_metrics.py),
keeping policy deterministic and unit-testable; [host_metrics.py](../../backend/app/services/host_metrics.py) turns collection failures into
unknown data so policy can fail open. None of these services owns `ExecutionEngine` behavior or
`AGENT.md` conventions, though [handoff_pipeline.py](../../backend/app/services/handoff_pipeline.py) calls app-side handoff agents.

## Shape

- [capacity_state.py](../../backend/app/services/capacity_state.py) â€” pure admission policy over timestamped CPU/memory readings plus the
  latest immutable snapshot/decision holder. It implements stale-data fail-open behavior,
  hysteresis, consecutive-breach confirmation, and minimum block duration; request paths only
  read its precomputed state.
- [host_metrics.py](../../backend/app/services/host_metrics.py) â€” boto3/IMDSv2 collection adapter. It resolves an override or tag-discovered
  EC2 inventory, obtains CloudWatch Agent readings, and returns an unknown-capacity snapshot
  rather than propagating AWS failure.
- [handoff_pipeline.py](../../backend/app/services/handoff_pipeline.py) â€” `run_handoff_pipeline()`, an async generator walking clone â†’ analyse â†’
  code â†’ test-report â†’ compliance â†’ commit â†’ push â†’ PR, yielding WS-shaped
  `{"type", "chunk", "section", "data"}` events consumed by the handoff route/WebSocket handler.
  Repo-walking helpers (`_walk_repo`, `_select_relevant_files`, `_select_test_files`) cap and
  filter the tree before it reaches the LLM; `_apply_edits`/`_safe_workspace_join` guard against
  path traversal when writing agent-produced edits back to the cloned workspace. Delegates git
  operations to `handoff_github` and coding/testing/compliance work to
  `app.agents.handoff.{CodingAgent,TestAgent,ComplianceAgent,classify_task}`.
- [handoff_github.py](../../backend/app/services/handoff_github.py) â€” URL parsing (HTTPS/SSH â†’ owner/repo), clone/push, and PR creation via the
  GitHub REST API directly (no `gh` CLI dependency). All `git` subprocess calls go through
  `_apply_child_rlimits` (POSIX rlimits: CPU/AS/FSIZE/NOFILE/NPROC) and `_build_git_env` (a
  scrubbed env â€” no inherited secrets, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so a failed PAT auth fails fast
  instead of hanging on a prompt) with a 90s wall-clock timeout.
- [od_loader.py](../../backend/app/services/od_loader.py) â€” reads `skills/opendesign/{design-templates,design-systems,craft}/` from disk
  (frontmatter + body via `_parse_frontmatter`), `lru_cache`d in-process. `_resolve_od_root()`
  tries, in order: `OD_ROOT` env override, the local-checkout relative path (`parents[3]` or
  `parents[2]`, covering both the local repo layout and the flattened container layout), then the
  baked container path `/app/opendesign`, then the legacy bind-mount `/app/skills/opendesign`.
- [pptx_export.py](../../backend/app/services/pptx_export.py) â€” extracts the `generatePresentation()` function from Agent 3's JS output and
  runs it in a Node.js subprocess to produce a real `.pptx`. Five defence-in-depth layers
  documented in the module docstring: syntactic sanitisation (quality only, not a security
  boundary), process isolation (scrubbed env + POSIX rlimits + `NODE_OPTIONS` heap cap + 0o700
  temp cwd + 120s wall-clock timeout decoupled from a 60s `RLIMIT_CPU`), a module-level
  `Semaphore` capping concurrent Node subprocesses at 3, container network egress restriction
  (enforced outside this file, at the VPC security-group level), and output size-capping /
  stderr path-redaction before any error reaches the HTTP response.

## Why this shape

Every service here treats its external input as attacker-influenced (LLM-produced JS for PPTX
export; a user-supplied PAT + repo URL for handoff) and **layers process-level isolation**
(rlimits, scrubbed env, timeouts, concurrency caps) rather than trusting sanitisation alone â€”
[pptx_export.py](../../backend/app/services/pptx_export.py)'s docstring is explicit that its regex fixups are for render-quality, not
security, and the real boundary is the subprocess sandbox plus network egress rules the
container enforces.

[handoff_github.py](../../backend/app/services/handoff_github.py) and [pptx_export.py](../../backend/app/services/pptx_export.py) share the identical rlimit/env-scrub subprocess pattern
independently rather than a shared abstraction, keeping each service's attack surface
self-contained and auditable in one file.

[od_loader.py](../../backend/app/services/od_loader.py)'s multi-path root resolution exists because the same code runs against three
different filesystem layouts (local checkout, flattened container image, EBS-mounted skills
volume) and picking the wrong one silently returns an empty template gallery rather than
erroring â€” so it tries every known layout in priority order instead of hardcoding one.

None of these services touch the `RunSandbox` or `deepagents` machinery in
`[MOD-backend-app-agents](MOD-backend-app-agents.md)`; they are deliberately kept as flat, single-purpose modules callable
from a route handler with no pipeline/agent-runtime coupling.
